A.explanation: Charge per unit time is the definition of electric current, $I = Q/t$, not potential difference.

B.explanation: Potential difference is defined as $V = W/Q$, the work done or energy transferred per unit charge passing through the component.

C.explanation: Force per unit charge defines electric field strength, $E = F/Q$, not potential difference.

D.explanation: Resistance per unit current has no physical meaning and does not give the unit volt, $	ext{J C}^{-1}$.

hints: Notice the question asks for potential difference across a component, measured in volts, not for how much charge flows each second.
Recall the governing relation $V = W/Q$ where $W$ is energy transferred and $Q$ is charge.
Compare each option's numerator to energy transferred: only one option has energy per coulomb of charge.
walkthrough: Identify what is asked: the formal definition of potential difference $V$ across a component, with unit volt.
State the physical rule: when charge $Q$ moves through a potential difference, work $W$ is done and energy is transferred, given by $V = W/Q$.
Check units: $1 \text{ V} = 1 \text{ J C}^{-1}$, so the definition must be energy per unit charge.
Eliminate the distractors: charge per unit time is current, force per unit charge is field strength, and resistance per unit current is not a defined quantity.
Therefore the energy transferred per unit charge matches $V = W/Q$. This is option B.
